result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): B caps the column at 72ch, a comfortable line length, and adds a 1rem gutter with min(). It shows only the new rule and explains why the header background still spans the full width. A's 960px cap still allows roughly 110 or more characters per line at 17px Georgia, so lines stay too long, and A repeats the whole stylesheet instead of showing only the change. Both keep code blocks scrollable and the header background full width. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): A sets the column with a 72ch cap, which gives a proper reading measure. It applies one centered column with a gutter to both `header .inner` and `main`, shows only the new rule, and explains why the header background still spans the full width. B's 960px cap at 17px Georgia allows lines of well over 100 characters, which is too wide. B also reprints the whole stylesheet instead of only the changes, though its padding approach works and the viewport meta tip is a useful extra.
